currentEtLStatus.advisoryStatus: Maine now loads official SOS certified President rows and town-level President-versus-U.S.-Senate review rows. Advisory indicators are source-review signals only, not findings of fraud or misconduct.

availableEvidence: The official 2024 results page lists U.S. President by County/Town (Excel).
The same page lists U.S. President by Congressional District (Excel), useful for Maine's split electoral-vote context.
The native Maine parser loads the official 2024 county/town workbook, and the separate local-geometry collector reads the same retained official rows for reviewed map joins.
certifiedResults.parserNeeded: Loaded by nativeMaineSosCountyTownXlsx from the official President by County/Town workbook. County totals plus State UOCAVA reconcile to 831,375 candidate votes; blank ballots remain source caveat context and are not candidate votes.
certifiedResults.caveat: State UOCAVA is loaded as a non-geographic certified result row and excluded from town/local map joins. Reviewed local-reporting geometry candidates remain fail-closed until immutable delivery and production review are completed.

Democratic/Republican dropoff metrics are directional source-review inputs. No normalized 2024 audit selection/outcome, recount disposition, incident, correction, or litigation rows are loaded.

remainingRisks: State UOCAVA is non-geographic: it is included in certified totals but not mapped or used in town review joins.
Three President town rows remain vote-share-only because the Senate workbook grain differs: Medway/Twps, Day Block Twp, and Wesley.
U.S. Senate includes a major independent candidate, so Democratic/Republican dropoff fields are directional source-review inputs only.
Turnout remains EAC fallback; collected Maine SOS active/inactive registered-enrolled files are denominator leads only until compatible ballots-cast or voter-participation rows are collected.
Reviewed local-reporting geometry/crosswalk candidates are not public until immutable delivery, database loading, and production activation are reviewed.

The 2012 municipal XLS is parsed for GIS, but five rows totaling eight votes lack unique geometry and the MGGG secondary reconstruction lacks confirmed exact official election-date applicability and explicit derivative redistribution permission.
Maine's source units are a mix of towns, plantations, townships, voting districts, and combined units; they must not be described as uniform precincts.
No normalized 2024 audit, recount, CVR availability, incident, correction, or litigation rows are loaded.
All advisory language must remain source-review context, not evidence of fraud or misconduct.
